title: Unified Inference: Q2 2026 Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Summary

This document consolidates the Q2 2026 product overview, high-level PRD, design specifications, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for the Unified Inference product. It is intended as the single source of truth for product, engineering, and go-to-market teams during the Q2 planning and release cycle.

1) Product overview 

Objective: Deliver a unified inference platform experience (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) that improves latency, lowers unit cost, and simplifies rollouts for engineering teams. Focus for Q2 2026: production-grade performance optimizations, refined pricing tiers, and improved rollout controls for model variants.

Key user personas:
- ML engineers: model onboarding, quantized variant management, perf profiling tools.
- Backend engineers: latency/cost SLOs, SDKs, autoscale policies.
- Platform teams: cross-team observability, reserved capacity allocation, and compliance controls.

Top-level success metrics (Q2 targets):
- Reduce average token cost for common chat workloads by 20% vs. Q1 baseline.
- P95 inference latency for small-medium sequence workloads (<= 512 tokens) <= 200ms for Hosted API.
- 99.9% availability SLA for Dedicated customer pools (measured monthly).
- Reach 5 new Dedicated customers on annual reserved contracts.

2) PRD: Goals, non-goals, and requirements

Goals (must have):
- Shipping automatic prefix/KV caching for chat workloads with an initial TTL policy and cache hit rate metrics (goal: 40% effective token saving on standard chat prompts).
- Improve batching heuristics to lower per-token CPU/GPU overhead for short requests while preserving tail latency SLOs.
- Update pricing tiers to reflect new per-token savings and introduce a Dedicated Starter tier for mid-market customers.

Non-goals (out of scope for Q2):
- Full private on-prem packaged installer (v2); only VPC-based Private deployment updates in scope.
- New model architecture support beyond current verified catalog (we will expand model catalog in parallel but not required for Q2 delivery).

Functional requirements (priority ordered):
1. Caching subsystem: 
   - Expose per-route caching toggles in Console and API.
   - Metrics: cache_hit_rate, tokens_saved_per_route, cache_evictions_per_minute.
   - TTL policy defaults: 10 minutes for chat prefix, 24 hours for embeddings cache.
2. Batching & routing: 
   - Dynamic batch size controller with latency guard: target average batching factor >= 3 without violating p95 latency SLO.
   - Smart routing policy: prefer lowest-cost compatible variant if p95 < threshold (200ms) else fallback to low-latency variant.
3. Pricing & packaging: 
   - Hosted API pricing tiers: Free (0-50k tokens/month), Developer (50k-5M tokens at baseline rate), Scale (committed volume; discount tiers).
   - Dedicated Starter: reserved-capacity SKU for predictable throughput up to 4 GPUs with SLA 99.9%; priced as monthly commitment with 6-month and 12-month options.
4. Observability & rollout controls: 
   - Per-model/per-route dashboards in Console with tokenized cost breakdowns and regressions alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
   - Canary and A/B rollout feature: percent-based traffic split and automatic rollback on quality regressions or latency breaks.

Non-functional requirements:
- Security: all data in transit encrypted (TLS 1.2+), default encryption at rest using customer-managed KMS for Private deployments.
- Scalability: service autoscaling to handle 3x peak Q1 traffic without manual capacity ops for Hosted tier.
- Reliability: error budget targets and automated fallbacks to secondary regions for critical customers.

Table: Acceptance criteria (pass/fail)
- Caching enabled and observed tokens_saved_per_route >= 30% for 3 sample customer workloads: PASS/FAIL
- Batch controller observes average batching factor >= 3 and p95 latency within target for 90% of traffic: PASS/FAIL
- Pricing changes published and billing pipeline validated end-to-end for Hosted/Scale customers: PASS/FAIL

3) Design spec (high-level)

Architecture overview:
- Components: API Gateway, Routing Service, Serving Runtime, KV/Prefix Cache, Batching Controller, Metrics Collector, Billing Pipeline, Console UI.
- Serving Runtime: GPU-optimized engine (existing runtime) with quantization-friendly paths and KV cache integration.
- Routing service: policy engine (latency/cost/region/tier) implemented as a stateless service with policy rules stored in Config Service.

Sequence: request flow (high-level)
1. Client -> API Gateway authenticates and validates request (rate limits and quotas checked).
2. Routing Service evaluates policy and selects model variant / region / capacity tier.
3. Batching Controller decides whether to batch the request (may queue briefly, 1-5ms).
4. Serving Runtime serves tokens, using KV/Prefix Cache when applicable.
5. Metrics Collector aggregates cost, latency, cache metrics and sends to observability pipeline.
6. Console renders per-route breakdowns and triggers alerts/rollouts if configured.

Design details & tradeoffs:
- Cache placement: adopt a hybrid memory + Redis cluster approach for high hit-rate prefixes. Tradeoff: Redis adds cost and cross-region latency- mitigate by routing cache-local traffic.
- Batching latency guard: small hold window (1-5ms) to increase batching factors. Tradeoff: slight added latency for tiny requests vs. improved economics- guarded by p95 SLO monitoring.

API and Console changes:
- API: new boolean query parameter cache_prefix=true/false; new fields returned in response metadata: cache_status (hit/miss), tokens_charged.
- Console: per-route toggle, cache metrics chart, and simplified pricing estimator.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Product: Sofia Martinez (PRD owner), roadmap and GTM messaging.
- Eng: Marcus Lee (serving runtime), Daniel Kim (routing & batching), Priya Rao (console & observability).
- SRE: capacity planning and runbooks.

4) Roadmap & themes (Q2 2026 top-level milestones)
- April 2026: Feature freeze for caching and batching core changes; integration tests complete.
- May 2026: Internal beta with 3 pilot customers (Hosted & Dedicated Starter); collect perf and billing telemetry.
- June 2026: General availability (GA) release; pricing updates go live; documentation and SDK updates published.

Quarter themes:
- Reliability & graceful degradation: improved fallbacks and multi-region routing test.
- Cost-aware performance: caching + batching improvements that reduce per-token cost.
- Enterprise readiness: Dedicated Starter SKUs and console controls for rollouts and auditing.

5) Pricing & packaging notes

Principles for pricing update:
- Transparent per-token economics: publish baseline per-token rates and show estimated savings from caching/quantization.
- Commitment discounts for scale customers: multi-tier discounts based on committed monthly token volumes and Dedicated capacity months.
- Simple entry path: keep Developer tier affordable to maintain PLG funnel.

Proposed pricing (illustrative; final list in pricing-approval doc):
- Free tier: 0-50k tokens / month, limited throughput, no SLA.
- Developer: 50k-5M tokens, $0.0008 / token (baseline, subject to rounding and unit definitions).
- Scale: > 5M tokens, volume discounts (5-25% depending on committed volume).
- Dedicated Starter: monthly commitment for reserved throughput up to 4x A100-equivalent GPUs, starting at $12,000 / month with 6-month and 12-month discounted options.

Billing & metering changes required:
- Add tokens_saved metric to billing pipeline to credit customer invoices when caching reduces billed tokens.
- Update billing pipeline to consume tokens_charged metadata from response path; reconcile with metrics collector for auditing.

GTM notes:
- Update pricing page and console estimator before GA.
- Sales enablement: one-pager for Dedicated Starter, comparison matrix vs. Dedicated Standard.

6) Release notes (v1.2 - Q2 2026 release candidate)

Release tag: unified-inference-v1.2-2026-06-15 (target GA date)
Highlights:
- Automatic prefix/KV caching for chat workloads with per-route toggle and cache metrics in Console.
- Dynamic batching controller with latency guard and configurable thresholds.
- Pricing updates: new Dedicated Starter SKU and revised Hosted pricing tiers (developer/scale).
- Console: per-route cost estimator and rollout controls (canary and percent-based splits).

Known limitations & mitigations:
- Cross-region cache misses may temporarily increase latency for remote customers. Mitigation: fallback to local low-latency variant and pre-warming rules.
- Billing reconciliation edge cases during beta: a manual auditing step will run for pilot customers until pipeline validations are complete.

Rollout plan:
1. Internal dogfood: 2 weeks, performance validation and observability stability checks.
2. Closed beta: 3 pilot customers (Hosted & Dedicated Starter) for 4 weeks; collect telemetry and adjust thresholds.
3. Gradual GA: enable for 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor errors/latency/regressions, then 50% for 72h, then 100% across non-sensitive accounts.

Rollback criteria (automated):
- If p95 latency increases > 25% vs baseline for > 30 minutes for > 10% of traffic, trigger automated rollback for affected route.
- If cache-related billing discrepancies > 1% for a major pilot customer, pause billing credits and roll back caching for that customer until reconciled.

7) Operational runbook highlights (summary)
- Playbooks: cache_eviction_spike, batch_controller_stall, routing_policy_misroute.
- Pager escalation: SRE on-call -> Eng-serving-runtime -> Product (owner) if rollout requires policy change.
- Key dashboards: p95 latency, cache_hit_rate by route, tokens_saved per customer, billing_reconciliations_failures.

8) Open decisions (to be resolved before feature freeze)
- Default TTL values for chat prefix cache (proposal: 10m) - owners: Marcus Lee & Priya Rao.
- Pricing per-token baseline numbers and rounding policy - owners: Finance & Product.
- Exact Dedicated Starter SKU configuration (GPU equivalence and burst capacity) - owners: Eng Infra & Product.

9) Next steps and owners
- Finalize cache TTL and policy matrix (Due: 2026-02-28) - Marcus Lee.
- Billing pipeline integration plan and audit checklist (Due: 2026-03-10) - Finance & Daniel Kim.
- Pilot recruitment and NDA sign-off for early customers (Due: 2026-03-15) - Sales & Customer Success.

Appendix: Commands, API examples, and sample configs

Example API (cache toggle):
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-13b","input":"Hello","cache_prefix":true}'

Example response metadata:
{
  "id": "req_123",
  "cache_status": "hit",
  "tokens_charged": 8
}

Console config sample (YAML):
route: customer-chat-route
enabled: true
cache_ttl: 600 # seconds
max_batch_delay_ms: 5
